verdict.rationale: Tavily is a web search, crawl and extract API, so a documented stance on robots.txt, content licensing and permitted use of results is a fair question for this product. No evidence item addresses robots.txt compliance, licensing of extracted content, or terms governing downstream use of results. The security and content-validation claim covers PII and prompt-injection filtering, which is a different feature and earns no credit here.

support.subject: As a data engineer, I can read a documented stance on robots.txt, content licensing, and permitted use of results
